## 7. Admission / born-promotion lifecycle (ratified: separate sequential classes)

| from | event | when | to |
|---|---|---|---|
| unadmitted | `admission` | disposition ∈ {child-proof-under-committed-outcome, separate-committed-outcome} | admitted-committed |
| unadmitted | `admission` | disposition ∈ {discovery, future-deferred} | admitted-parked |
| unadmitted | `admission` | disposition = duplicate-superseded-disposed | admitted-disposed |
| unadmitted | `admission` | disposition = hold | admitted-hold |
| admitted-parked | `born-promotion` | prior admission disposition ∈ {discovery, future-deferred} | promoted-committed-outcome |

**Invariant:** A born-promotion event for a workId is valid ONLY when a prior non-revoked admission event exists for that workId whose disposition is a PROMOTABLE state — exactly {discovery, future-deferred} (→ lifecycle state 'admitted-parked'). A 'duplicate-superseded-disposed' admission is terminal ('admitted-disposed') and can NEVER be promoted; 'admitted-committed' and 'admitted-hold' are likewise non-promotable. born-promotion supersedes nothing; it is a forward transition. Phase-4 proves this with a state-transition test BEFORE any ledger write; if the invariant cannot be shown, the ledger stays unwritten (typed HOLD).
